slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will pull you out
of your dopamine addiction

birdwatching

sit in a park for twenty minutes and try to spot five different birds. waiting for something slow and real slowly retrains a brain that got used to instant rewards.

baking bread

bake one loaf a week from scratch. kneading, waiting and checking the oven teaches your brain to enjoy rewards that take hours to arrive instead of seconds.

handwritten letters

write one letter by hand each month to someone you care about. slow communication feels strange at first, then it becomes the most meaningful part of your week.

swapping one scroll

every time you reach for a feed, learn one real thing instead: a planet, a painting, a moment in history. small real rewards slowly replace the empty ones.

long walks with no plan

walk for an hour with no music and no destination once a week. the first fifteen minutes feel boring, and then your mind finally starts to wander freely.
